routes.label: Find the area of one face

question:
Isaiah cuts open a cardboard cube along some of its edges to form the flat shape shown, which has an area of \(18\) square centimeters. What was the volume of the cube in cubic centimeters?

[Figure 1](figures/2025_AMC_8_Q08_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The net contains all six square faces of the cube without overlap. Cutting and unfolding rearrange these faces without changing their areas, so each face has area \(18\div6=3\) square centimeters.

Let \(s>0\) be the cube's edge length in centimeters. A square face has area \(s^2\), so \(s^2=3\) and \(s=\sqrt3\). Multiplying the area of a face by the perpendicular edge length gives the volume:
\[
V=s^2\cdot s=3\sqrt3\text{ cubic centimeters}.
\]
The answer is \(3\sqrt3\) cubic centimeters, choice A.
